nominations.contribution: for the analysis of nominal rigidities and the design of monetary policy rules in dynamic general equilibrium
key_works: Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
Calvo, 1983: Staggered Prices in a Utility-Maximizing Framework, Journal of Monetary Economics
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: The New Keynesian framework is the workhorse of central-bank modelling: staggered pricing (Taylor, Calvo) gave a tractable mechanism and Woodford built a coherent welfare-based theory of interest-rate policy on it. It meets the test of a clear core idea that changed both research and policy practice. The main reservation is attribution within a broad literature and doubt about how robust its predictions are at the zero lower bound.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of credit constraints and collateral as amplifiers of business cycles
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: A simple dynamic equilibrium mechanism, in which asset prices and borrowing capacity feed back on each other, became the core of post-2008 macro-finance models. Its general-equilibrium feedback loop is exactly the kind of tractable insight that reshapes quantitative modelling. It partly overlaps with the 2022 prize to Bernanke on financial frictions, but it is a distinct theoretical contribution.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of public debt, Ricardian equivalence and tax smoothing in dynamic macroeconomics
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro, 1979: On the Determination of the Public Debt, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Barro brought intertemporal optimization to fiscal policy and set the benchmark that all later analysis of deficits and debt management departs from. Tax smoothing is a clean, general result with lasting policy content. The reservation is that Ricardian equivalence is mainly valued as a benchmark rather than as an empirical description.

nominations.contribution: for the intertemporal theory of consumption under rational expectations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Euler-equation approach turned consumption theory into a testable dynamic restriction and created the template for estimating intertemporal models. It is a sharply attributable idea with enormous methodological reach. The reservation is that it builds on the work already rewarded to Friedman and Modigliani.

nominations.contribution: for the development of incomplete-markets models with heterogeneous agents in macroeconomics
key_works: Bewley, 1986: Stationary Monetary Equilibrium with a Continuum of Independently Fluctuating Consumers, in Contributions to Mathematical Economics
Huggett, 1993: The Risk-Free Rate in Heterogeneous-Agent Incomplete-Insurance Economies, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
nominations.rationale: Bewley-type models are now the workhorse for distributional macro and fiscal policy analysis. They allow quantitative welfare analysis with uninsured risk. The main reservation is attribution: the key developer, Aiyagari, is deceased and other contributors are close to the committee.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy rules
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus policy rules in practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series
Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The science of monetary policy, Journal of Economic Literature
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: These works give clean, implementable policy rules, and central banks have adopted them, which is the theory-to-institution bridge I value. The main reservation is attribution, since Gertler, Clarida and Rotemberg also shaped the framework.

nominations.contribution: for showing how credit constraints and collateral amplify and propagate business cycles
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is a conceptually deep mechanism with a clear, general logic that travels well beyond one setting. It partly overlaps with the 2022 financial-intermediation prize.

nominations.contribution: for contributions to dynamic macroeconomic methods and the analysis of fluctuations and stabilization policy
key_works: Blanchard and Kahn, 1980: The solution of linear difference models under rational expectations, Econometrica
Blanchard and Kiyotaki, 1987: Monopolistic competition and the effects of aggregate demand, American Economic Review
Blanchard and Quah, 1989: The dynamic effects of aggregate demand and supply disturbances, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The contribution is broad and foundational in its tools. It is less a single crisp result than a body of work.

nominations.contribution: for the intertemporal analysis of consumption and of government debt under rational expectations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic implications of the life cycle-permanent income hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Barro, 1974: Are government bonds net wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Both papers are sharp, testable theoretical propositions that reshaped consumption and fiscal analysis. The reservation is that they partly overlap with the Friedman and Modigliani prizes.

nominations.contribution: for integrating household heterogeneity into monetary and fiscal policy analysis
key_works: Kaplan, Moll and Violante, 2018: Monetary policy according to HANK, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This approach is transforming the field. The work is young, so the prize is premature now.

nominations.contribution: for the development of the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy rules
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus policy rules in practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The science of monetary policy: a New Keynesian perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: This framework has become the working model of central banks, and the Taylor-rule description of policy has held up across many countries and samples. It is a cumulative program, not a single striking result. My reservation is that the empirical support for some microfoundations, such as Calvo pricing and the forward-looking Phillips curve, is weaker than the framework's policy influence suggests.

nominations.contribution: for the narrative identification of the macroeconomic effects of monetary and fiscal policy
key_works: Romer and Romer, 2004: A new measure of monetary shocks: derivation and implications, American Economic Review
Romer and Romer, 2010: The macroeconomic effects of tax changes: estimates based on a new measure of fiscal shocks, American Economic Review
Ramey, 2011: Identifying government spending shocks: it's all in the timing, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: These authors built transparent, documented shock series that others can rebuild, scrutinize and extend, and that is exactly the kind of credibility revolution I value in macro. The resulting estimates have been re-examined across countries and periods. Multiplier estimates remain sensitive to specification, but the authors have been unusually open about that sensitivity.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of credit constraints and collateral in the propagation of business cycles

people.name: John Moore
people.affiliation: University of Edinburgh and London School of Economics

key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Credit cycles became central to post-2008 macroeconomics and provide a clear, falsifiable mechanism for amplification. The theory has been widely built upon. Direct quantitative tests of its strength have produced mixed results, which I would want weighed.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of public debt, Ricardian equivalence and the intertemporal effects of fiscal policy
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are government bonds net wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro, 1979: On the determination of the public debt, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Barro's work set the benchmark against which every fiscal policy analysis is still tested. It is a theoretical claim that has been genuinely confronted with data. Most of that evidence rejects strict Ricardian equivalence, so the case for the prize rests on its value as a benchmark.

nominations.contribution: for integrating household heterogeneity into the analysis of monetary and fiscal policy
key_works: Kaplan, Moll and Violante, 2018: Monetary policy according to HANK, American Economic Review
Kaplan and Violante, 2014: A model of fiscal stimulus, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: These models discipline macro with micro evidence on marginal propensities to consume, and that evidence has replicated well across countries. The program has rapidly changed how policy transmission is studied. It is still young, and the authors are early relative to the usual age of laureates.

nominations.contribution: for the development of the New Keynesian framework for monetary policy analysis
key_works: Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Galí and Gertler, 1999: Inflation Dynamics: A Structural Econometric Analysis, Journal of Monetary Economics
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: This framework changed how central banks design and evaluate policy, and it links micro-founded theory to welfare-based policy rules. The empirical identification of the Phillips curve remains contested, which is my main reservation.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of credit constraints and collateral in the propagation of macroeconomic fluctuations
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is an original mechanism showing how small shocks are amplified through asset prices and borrowing limits, and it became central after 2008. It is close to the 2022 banking prize but remains distinct from it.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of rules-based monetary policy
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Taylor rule is a rare case of research that directly reshaped how policy is evaluated. It is more a policy benchmark than a deep structural contribution.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the intertemporal effects of fiscal policy and the credibility of monetary policy
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro and Gordon, 1983: Rules, Discretion and Reputation in a Model of Monetary Policy, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: Ricardian equivalence and the credibility analysis defined decades of debate on fiscal and monetary policy. The overlap with the 2004 time-consistency prize weakens the case.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of consumption dynamics and labor-market fluctuations under rational expectations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The Euler-equation approach transformed empirical consumption analysis. His work on unemployment volatility bridges search theory and macro. The contribution is broad rather than a single defining breakthrough.

nominations.contribution: for showing how credit frictions and collateral constraints amplify and propagate macroeconomic fluctuations
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist, 1999: The Financial Accelerator in a Quantitative Business Cycle Framework, Handbook of Macroeconomics
Gertler and Kiyotaki, 2010: Financial Intermediation and Credit Policy in Business Cycle Analysis, Handbook of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: This work takes incomplete-contracting ideas in the Hart–Moore tradition into macroeconomics, and it gives a precise mechanism linking collateral, leverage and real activity. It has become the standard framework for macro-financial policy after 2008. The main reservation is overlap with Bernanke's 2022 prize, but the collateral-cycle mechanism is a distinct contribution.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy
key_works: Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Galí, 2008: Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle, Princeton University Press
Blanchard and Kiyotaki, 1987: Monopolistic Competition and the Effects of Aggregate Demand, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This is the workhorse framework of modern central banking, built on rigorous microfoundations. Its influence on policy practice is enormous. Its empirical validation is weaker than its theoretical elegance.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of rules-based monetary policy
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Taylor rule is a durable institutional benchmark used directly by central banks. Taylor's staggered-contracts work also models price-setting institutions realistically. It is close to the 2004 time-consistency prize but distinct from it.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of government debt, Ricardian equivalence and the macroeconomics of fiscal policy
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro, 1979: On the Determination of the Public Debt, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Barro reshaped how economists reason about deficits and tax smoothing. The work is foundational and broadly influential. Empirical support for strict equivalence is limited.

nominations.contribution: for the rational-expectations analysis of consumption and labor market dynamics
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Hall's random-walk result set out a sharp, testable mechanism that founded modern empirical consumption research. It is a strong case of confronting theory with data. Part of this ground overlaps the earlier Friedman and Modigliani prizes.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework of nominal rigidities and interest-rate rules for monetary policy analysis
key_works: Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
Calvo, 1983: Staggered Prices in a Utility-Maximizing Framework, Journal of Monetary Economics
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: This is the workhorse of central banks and of modern business-cycle theory. It is built on optimizing foundations that aggregate cleanly. The reservation is that its empirical fit relies on ad hoc frictions, and that its representative-agent core is now being revised.

nominations.contribution: for the development of heterogeneous-agent incomplete-markets macroeconomics and methods for solving it with aggregate shocks
key_works: Bewley, 1986: Stationary Monetary Equilibrium with a Continuum of Independently Fluctuating Consumers, in Contributions to Mathematical Economics
Krusell and Smith, 1998: Income and Wealth Heterogeneity in the Macroeconomy, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: These methods made distributional macroeconomics quantitatively tractable, and they are now standard tools. Because of my close collaboration with Krusell, I would have to recuse myself from deliberating on this nomination.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of public debt neutrality and the credibility of monetary policy rules
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro and Gordon, 1983: A Positive Theory of Monetary Policy in a Natural Rate Model, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Ricardian equivalence and the inflation-bias framework are benchmarks that every fiscal and monetary analysis confronts. The reservation is that part of this work overlaps with the 2004 time-consistency prize.

nominations.contribution: for showing how credit constraints and collateral values amplify and propagate business cycles
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is an elegant general-equilibrium mechanism that became central after 2008. The question is how large the amplification is quantitatively, which remains debated.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of consumption under rational expectations and of labor-market fluctuations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The Euler-equation approach to consumption transformed empirical macroeconomics. The reservation is that his contribution is spread across many topics rather than concentrated in one.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for monetary policy analysis
key_works: Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Galí, 2008: Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: This is the workhorse of modern central banking and unites theory with policy practice. The authorship and influence are clear. My reservation is that its empirical validation rests mostly on postwar data from advanced economies rather than on long historical regimes.

nominations.contribution: for showing how credit constraints and collateral amplify and propagate economic fluctuations
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: It is a deep mechanism linking asset prices, land and credit to cycles. The mechanism maps well onto historical boom-bust episodes, including property-driven crises in the Nordics. It is distinct from the 2022 award on banks.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of monetary policy rules and their role in macroeconomic stabilization
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Taylor rule became a universal benchmark for describing and evaluating policy, including retrospectively across historical regimes. Staggered contracts also helped found modern nominal-rigidity models. It overlaps partly with the New Keynesian nomination above.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of international monetary regimes, the gold standard and the propagation of the Great Depression
key_works: Eichengreen, 1992: Golden Fetters: The Gold Standard and the Great Depression, 1919-1939, Oxford University Press
Eichengreen and Sachs, 1985: Exchange Rates and Economic Recovery in the 1930s, Journal of Economic History
nominations.rationale: It is a model of historically grounded macroeconomics, using cross-country variation in leaving gold to identify monetary effects. Its findings are confirmed across many countries and periods. It might be seen as partly overlapping with Friedman's monetary history and with Bernanke.

nominations.contribution: for the rational-expectations analysis of consumption and contributions to the measurement of business cycles
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The random-walk consumption result transformed empirical consumption research. Hall's broad empirical macro has also been durable. The main reservation is closeness to the already awarded Friedman and Modigliani consumption work.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy
key_works: Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Galí and Gertler, 1999: Inflation Dynamics: A Structural Econometric Analysis, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: This framework durably changed both modelling and central-bank practice by building policy analysis on optimizing firms that set prices under rigidities. The firm-pricing microfoundations match my own lens. My reservation is that its Calvo-type pricing block is stylized relative to what micro price data show, and credit must be shared with Clarida.

nominations.contribution: for establishing the microeconomic evidence on price setting and its implications for monetary non-neutrality
key_works: Bils and Klenow, 2004: Some Evidence on the Importance of Sticky Prices, Journal of Political Economy
Nakamura and Steinsson, 2008: Five Facts about Prices: A Reevaluation of Menu Cost Models, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Klenow and Kryvtsov, 2008: State-Dependent or Time-Dependent Pricing, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This is exactly what I value: macro theory confronted with price data at the level where firms decide, which reshaped how price rigidity is modelled. My reservations are that the contribution is young and that credit is spread across many authors, including Steinsson and Kryvtsov.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of how credit constraints and collateral amplify and propagate business cycles
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is a clean mechanism linking firms' balance sheets to aggregate fluctuations, and it became central after 2008. My reservation is that the 2022 prize (Bernanke) is partly adjacent, and that direct micro identification of the mechanism remains limited.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of staggered price setting and of rules for monetary policy
key_works: Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
Calvo, 1983: Staggered Prices in a Utility-Maximizing Framework, Journal of Monetary Economics
Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series
nominations.rationale: These are the originators of the contract-staggering devices and of the policy rule that dominate practice. There is substantial overlap with the rank-1 contribution, so the two would probably be considered as alternatives.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of consumption under rational expectations and of the macroeconomic effects of fiscal policy
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Both papers transformed empirical testing in consumption and fiscal analysis. My reservation is that the pairing is somewhat loose and that the area builds on contributions already awarded to Friedman and Modigliani.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy
key_works: Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist, 1999: The Financial Accelerator in a Quantitative Business Cycle Framework, Handbook of Macroeconomics
nominations.rationale: This is the framework central banks actually use, so it shapes a real institution. My main question is how to share credit within a large community: Clarida is also central, and the empirical identification of the model's key parameters is still debated.

nominations.contribution: for narrative identification of the effects of monetary and fiscal policy
key_works: Romer and Romer, 1989: Does Monetary Policy Matter? A New Test in the Spirit of Friedman and Schwartz, NBER Macroeconomics Annual
Romer and Romer, 2004: A New Measure of Monetary Shocks: Derivation and Implications, American Economic Review
Romer and Romer, 2010: The Macroeconomic Effects of Tax Changes, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They built new shock measures from archival policy records and brought design-based reasoning into macroeconomics, which closely matches my own priorities. One reservation is whether the narrative shocks are truly exogenous; another is that the contribution is mainly methodological rather than a broad theory.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of rules-based monetary policy
key_works: Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Taylor rule became a standard benchmark for both central banks and researchers, a clear case of influence on how an institution operates. It overlaps with the New Keynesian nomination, and the two could be combined.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of nominal rigidities, monopolistic competition and aggregate demand

key_works: Blanchard and Kiyotaki, 1987: Monopolistic Competition and the Effects of Aggregate Demand, American Economic Review
Blanchard and Quah, 1989: The Dynamic Effects of Aggregate Demand and Supply Disturbances, American Economic Review
Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: They supplied the microfoundations behind modern models of aggregate demand. The contribution is broad but somewhat diffuse, and Kiyotaki's strongest claim may lie in Finance.

nominations.contribution: for contributions to the theory and empirics of consumption and labor-market fluctuations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The random-walk consumption result was a turning point for testable macroeconomics. His later contributions are spread across many topics, which makes a single citation harder to write.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy and business cycles
key_works: Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist, 1999: The Financial Accelerator in a Quantitative Business Cycle Framework, Handbook of Macroeconomics
nominations.rationale: This framework is the common language of central banks worldwide, so its influence on policy institutions is unusually direct and lasting. Inflation targeting by independent central banks is an institutional design question I find compelling. My reservation is how far the model is supported empirically outside the advanced-economy post-war sample.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of credit constraints and collateral as propagators of economic fluctuations
key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is an elegant mechanism linking property rights over collateral to aggregate dynamics, and it became central after 2008. It fits well with the institutional view of how contract enforcement shapes macro outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for the formulation of simple monetary policy rules and the analysis of staggered wage and price setting
key_works: Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
nominations.rationale: The Taylor rule is a rare case of a transparent, measurable rule that disciplines policy institutions and became a benchmark across countries. It is partly anticipated by the 2004 time-consistency prize.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of government debt, fiscal policy and the credibility of macroeconomic policy
key_works: Barro, 1974: Are Government Bonds Net Wealth?, Journal of Political Economy
Barro and Gordon, 1983: Rules, Discretion and Reputation in a Model of Monetary Policy, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: Barro's work on Ricardian equivalence and on reputational policy games links macroeconomics to political economy. His cross-country work on democracy and growth also engaged political science directly. A drawback is overlap with the 2004 laureates.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of consumption under rational expectations and of labour market fluctuations
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The random-walk consumption result changed empirical macro practice. Hall also contributed to the measurement and dating of business cycles. It is a solid but more narrowly macro contribution, further from my institutional concerns.

nominations.contribution: for developing the New Keynesian framework for the analysis of monetary policy
key_works: Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices, Princeton University Press
Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective, Journal of Economic Literature
Galí and Gertler, 1999: Inflation Dynamics: A Structural Econometric Analysis, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: This is the workhorse of central banks and of academic monetary analysis: an internally consistent dynamic general-equilibrium model that supports welfare-based policy evaluation. Woodford supplied the welfare foundations and the theory of optimal policy, and Galí and Gertler supplied the empirical and policy-rule discipline. My main reservation is that the representative-agent core and the weak empirical fit of the Phillips curve leave open questions that heterogeneous-agent work is now addressing.

nominations.contribution: for showing how credit constraints and collateral amplify and propagate macroeconomic fluctuations

people.affiliation: University of Edinburgh and London School of Economics

key_works: Kiyotaki and Moore, 1997: Credit Cycles, Journal of Political Economy
Kiyotaki and Moore, 2019: Liquidity, Business Cycles, and Monetary Policy, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The paper gives a clean equilibrium mechanism, in which asset prices and collateral feed back into investment, and it has become the foundation of macro-finance models used after 2008. It survives the general-equilibrium test because the amplification comes from price feedback itself. The quantitative size of the amplification in calibrated versions remains debated.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of consumption under rational expectations and of labor-market dynamics in equilibrium macroeconomics
key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The Euler-equation approach to consumption transformed empirical macro and remains the starting point of every intertemporal consumption model. His later work on wage rigidity in search models sharpened the unemployment-volatility debate. The contribution is spread across several areas, which makes a sharp motivation harder to write.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of staggered price setting and of rules for monetary policy
key_works: Taylor, 1980: Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts, Journal of Political Economy
Taylor, 1993: Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy
nominations.rationale: Staggered contracts and the Taylor rule became durable tools that are used in essentially every monetary model and in central-bank practice. The rule was introduced as a positive description and only later received normative foundations from others. That makes it an alternative to, rather than a complement of, the New Keynesian nomination.

nominations.contribution: for integrating household heterogeneity and incomplete markets into the analysis of monetary and fiscal policy
key_works: Kaplan, Moll and Violante, 2018: Monetary Policy According to HANK, American Economic Review
Kaplan and Violante, 2014: A Model of the Consumption Response to Fiscal Stimulus Payments, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: HANK has changed how the transmission of policy is understood, shifting it from intertemporal substitution to indirect general-equilibrium income effects, and it is rapidly becoming a workhorse. The computational methods built on earlier incomplete-markets tools, which raises questions of attribution relative to predecessors. The laureates would also be young by historical standards.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of monetary policy in New Keynesian dynamic general-equilibrium models with nominal rigidities
key_works: Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 1999: "The Science of Monetary Policy: A New Keynesian Perspective", Journal of Economic Literature
Woodford, 2003: Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press
Galí, 2008: Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: This is the post-Lucas workhorse framework through which central banks and macroeconomists organize nominal rigidities, expectations, welfare losses and interest-rate rules. The attribution is clear, and the framework is both analytically tractable and quantitatively usable. The reservation is that parts of the framework became standard through a broad community and its empirical fit has been repeatedly challenged.

nominations.contribution: for the development of heterogeneous-agent incomplete-market macroeconomics and its implications for saving, inequality and aggregate dynamics
key_works: Bewley, 1986: "Stationary Monetary Equilibrium with a Continuum of Independently Fluctuating Consumers", in Contributions to Mathematical Economics in Honor of Gérard Debreu
Huggett, 1993: "The Risk-Free Rate in Heterogeneous-Agent Incomplete-Insurance Economies", Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
Krusell and Smith, 1998: "Income and Wealth Heterogeneity in the Macroeconomy", Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The Bewley-Huggett-Krusell-Smith line changed macroeconomics by putting uninsured idiosyncratic risk, wealth distributions and aggregate shocks into equilibrium models. It is now central to monetary and fiscal policy analysis because distributional states matter for aggregate dynamics. The main reservation is that a deceased contributor, Aiyagari, is also central to the canonical formulation and cannot be named.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of monopolistic competition, nominal rigidities and coordination failures in aggregate fluctuations

people.name: Olivier Blanchard
people.affiliation: Peterson Institute for International Economics and Massachusetts Institute of Technology

key_works: Blanchard and Kiyotaki, 1987: "Monopolistic Competition and the Effects of Aggregate Demand", American Economic Review
Kiyotaki, 1988: "Multiple Expectational Equilibria under Monopolistic Competition", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Blanchard and Fischer, 1989: Lectures on Macroeconomics, MIT Press

key_works: Hall, 1978: Stochastic Implications of the Life Cycle-Permanent Income Hypothesis: Theory and Evidence, Journal of Political Economy
Hall, 2005: Employment Fluctuations with Equilibrium Wage Stickiness, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: He has repeatedly provided durable, tractable frameworks for analyzing macroeconomic outcomes, from consumption under uncertainty to search-matching in general equilibrium. His work establishes tight links between dynamic theory and empirical moments. However, his frameworks often rely on specific functional or behavioral assumptions that can be sensitive to aggregate shocks.

nominations.contribution: for his quantitative analysis of income dynamics, heterogeneity, and inequality in macroeconomics
key_works: Guvenen, 2007: Learning Your Earning: Are Labor Income Shocks Really Very Persistent?, American Economic Review
Guvenen et al., 2014: The Nature of Countercyclical Income Risk, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: He has pushed the frontier of incomplete-market macroeconomics by tightly linking massive micro-datasets on income risk to quantitative dynamic models. His work answers precisely how individual heterogeneity and non-Gaussian shocks aggregate into macroeconomic outcomes. One might question if the field has fully converged on how best to model this higher-order risk in a full general-equilibrium setting.

nominations.contribution: for her empirical contributions to the measurement of macroeconomic shocks and government spending multipliers
key_works: Ramey, 2011: Identifying Government Spending Shocks: It's all in the Timing, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Her work disciplines quantitative macro models by providing highly credible, rigorously measured estimates of fiscal policy and technology shocks. She forces structural modelers to confront true empirical magnitudes. Although her contributions are largely empirical, they are foundational for anyone calibrating dynamic general-equilibrium models.
